newsitem.title: ABU DHABI: UAE protests to Iran over naval "violation".
newsitem.headline: UAE protests to Iran over naval "violation".

text.p: The United Arab Emirates on Tuesday protested to Iran about the alleged unauthorised entry of an Iranian naval vessel into UAE waters, the official WAM news agency said.

"The naval vessel crossed into UAE territorial waters on January 19 without receiving prior permission from the authorities, in order to tow a small vessel carrying cement, building materials and cars," WAM said.
It did not say how long the ships were in UAE waters or where they were headed.

UAE acting Foreign Ministry undersecretary Seif bin Said delivered a letter of protest to Iran's ambassador in Abu Dhabi, Hossein Sadiqi, which urged Iran to avoid such transgressions in the future, WAM said.

"(The letter) called on Iran not to repeat these unjustified violations...saying it has a negative impact on relations between the two neighbouring Moslem countries and on commitments to international norms and principles of good neighbourliness, which govern relations between states," the agency said.
Relations between the UAE and non-Arab Iran, neighbours across the Gulf, have been strained for years over a territorial dispute concerning three Gulf islands.
In 1992 the UAE accused Iran of occupying the islands of Greater and Lesser Tunb and Abu Musa and revived its territorial claim after Iran tightened security measures at Abu Musa.
The UAE has urged Iran to take the row to the International Court of Justice. Iran says its sovereignty over the islands is not negotiable and has called for bilateral talks.
